title: Claims Desk Points of Judgement — Filing a Claim on the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans
content:
The filing conditions of the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans, answered as the questions the claims desk decides.

## The conditions

A claim is filed against a plan standing in active or pending renewal status, never against suspended cover, and it names the unit, the component and the work order the fault was found on. The claim must be filed no later than the tier's filing period counted forward in calendar days from the day the fault was found, the day of discovery excluded and the final day included; a claim filed later is denied for late filing however plainly the fault is covered. Where the estimated repair passes the tier's prior authorisation threshold, the claim is authorised before the work starts, and work started without that authorisation is paid only up to the threshold. The claim must also show maintenance: the last documented maintenance visit on the unit must fall inside the tier's proof of maintenance period before the fault was found.

## Against which plan may a claim be filed?

Against a plan whose record shows the status active or pending renewal. A plan in suspended status takes no claim. It is the plan record's status that decides, read for the plan the claim is filed against.

## What must the claim name?

The unit that failed, the component the claim concerns, and the service work order on which the fault was found.

## When is a claim filed in time?

Within the tier's filing period, counted forward in calendar days from the day the fault was found: the day of discovery is day zero and is not counted, each following calendar day is counted, and the final day of the period is a timely filing day. A claim filed after the final day is denied for late filing, whatever the merit of the fault.

| Tier | Filing period | Fault found (hypothetical) | Last timely filing day | Filed on | Timely |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compressor Coverage Plan | 21 calendar days | 3 June | 24 June | 24 June | Yes |
| Compressor Coverage Plan | 21 calendar days | 3 June | 24 June | 25 June | No — denied for late filing |
| Total Equipment Protection Plan | 14 calendar days | 3 June | 17 June | 17 June | Yes |
| Parts Protection Plan | 30 calendar days | 3 June | 3 July | 4 July | No — denied for late filing |

The day the fault was found is the day the claim record carries as the fault-found day.

## When must the repair be authorised before work starts?

Where the estimated repair exceeds the tier's prior authorisation threshold. Work started without that authorisation, where authorisation was required, is paid only up to the threshold.

- Estimated repair of 1400 USD on the Compressor Coverage Plan (threshold 1000 USD): authorisation before work starts is required; started without it, the claim pays no more than 1000 USD.
- Estimated repair of 900 USD on the same tier does not exceed 1000 USD, and the authorisation condition of this clause is not triggered by it.

## What maintenance must the claim show?

That the last documented maintenance visit on the unit falls inside the tier's proof of maintenance period, counted back in calendar months from the day the fault was found. A visit outside that period does not satisfy the condition.

- Major Component Protection Plan, proof period 6 calendar months, fault found 10 September: a documented visit on 20 April falls inside; the last documented visit on 2 February does not.

## The tier figures these conditions read

The filing period in calendar days, the prior authorisation threshold in USD and the proof of maintenance period in calendar months are the tier's own figures under the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans.
